title: IED Kills Six Lawyers, Wounds 22 at Damascus Cafe Near Palace of Justice
detail: An improvised explosive device planted under a table at the Al-Mushairiya Cafe on al-Nasr Street in Damascus's al-Hijaz district detonated on July 2, 2026, killing at least nine people — including six lawyers (Mohannad Khalaf, Mahmoud Shehab, Eid Mohammad, Fathi Al-Qabbani, Mohammad Shamali, and Hossam Al-Safadi) — and wounding 22. The cafe sits roughly 70 metres from the Palace of Justice, a popular gathering spot for legal professionals, and is located near the courthouse currently trying prominent former Assad-era officials, including ex-security chief Atef Najib. No group claimed responsibility; the local governor said 'bad actors' were trying to destabilize the country. Investigators said the bomber planted the device and left, possibly intending further attacks at the courthouse itself.

title: Renewed Clashes Between Druze National Guard and Government Forces in Suwayda
detail: Heavy clashes broke out between the Druze-led National Guard and Syrian government forces in the Tal al-Hadid area west of Suwayda city late on July 2, continuing into the morning of July 3, 2026. At least two people were killed and dozens injured. State-run Al-Ikhbariah TV said gunmen attacked government security positions in the area; government forces reinforced their presence over the following days amid sporadic exchanges of fire. The clashes mark the most serious escalation since the ceasefire agreed between Damascus and local Druze leaders in July 2025, following the deadly Suwayda violence of that summer that the SOHR said killed over 1,300 people.
